title: Normalized coefficient encoding and a fixed compactification
statement: For a finite discrete commutative ring A, any family E of normalized Encodings from [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding], any scheme morphism f:X->Y, and any specified compactification c of f, there is a natural isomorphism from CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c followed by (E Y).fixedDerived to (E X).fixedDerived followed by the fixed ModuleCat(ULift A) rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification c. Both functors use the very same c; no alternative compactification or completion is used.

proof.text: For $h:U\to T$, both underived direct images have section group $M(V\times_TU)$ on $V\in T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]; [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and, through step 3, [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]). In the internal construction the scalar acts through $\eta_h$; in the ordinary construction it acts through the constant-ring restriction. The equation in the universe-general canonicalAbelianMap_naturality of [lem-sf-finite-discrete-encoding-naturality] identifies these actions, so the identity on the section groups gives a natural isomorphism $E_Th_*\cong h_*E_U$. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, step 8 identifies internal $j^*$ with the ordinary module pullback, which for an open immersion is restriction $(j^*G)(W\to U)=G(W\to U\to T)$, the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] read through step 3. The exact internal $j_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and the ordinary $j_!$ of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] (the one used in [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification]) are both left adjoint to these, by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. They are therefore identified by their Hom bijections: $\operatorname{Hom}(E_Tj_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*E_T^{-1}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E_UM,j^*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!E_UM,N)$. The bijections are natural and their identity transposes give inverse isomorphisms.

source.place: Module pushforward and adjunction with open restriction; the section-action equality and explicit adjoint Hom bijections

proof.text: The exact equivalences $E_U,E_T$ preserve K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since each is right adjoint to its exact inverse. Given any complex $M$ on $U$, choose an internal K-injective resolution $M\to I$. Then $E_UM\to E_UI$ is an ordinary K-injective resolution. Compute the two derived direct images on these representatives: step 11 gives $E_T(h_*I)\cong h_*(E_UI)$ termwise, hence $D(E_T)Rh_*\cong Rh_*D(E_U)$ naturally on the unbounded categories, using [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The exact $j_!$ comparison from step 11 applies termwise. For the fixed compactification $c=(j,p)$, compose these two comparisons to obtain $D(E_Y)Rp_*D(j_!)\cong Rp_*j_!D(E_X)$. These are exactly the two composites defined in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification]. No compactification change or etale/pro-etale comparison is used.

lean.statement:
theorem encoding_compactification [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A]
    (E : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Encoding A T)
    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification f) :
    Nonempty (CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c ⋙
        (E Y).fixedDerived.functor ≅
      (E X).fixedDerived.functor ⋙
        rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)) c)
